faq.q: What is the weather like in Marbella in August?
faq.a: August in Marbella is hot and dry. Expect daytime highs of 30-34°C, with occasional peaks above 36°C. The sea water is warm, around 24-26°C, making swimming very pleasant. The breeze on the water can make it feel 5-8°C cooler than on land.

faq.q: Which boat is best for staying cool in August?
faq.a: Flybridge boats like the Azimut 58 Flybridge or the Ferretti 94 are ideal because they offer shaded upper decks with better airflow. The Mangusta 80 also has a large flybridge and a spacious saloon with air conditioning, perfect for escaping the midday sun.

faq.q: What time of day should I rent a boat in August?
faq.a: To avoid the peak heat, book a morning charter (9:00-13:00) or a late afternoon one (16:00-20:00). Midday charters are still popular but you'll need to use the boat's shade and take regular swims to cool off.

faq.q: Are drinks and snacks included on the boat?
faq.a: Yes, every charter includes water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. You can also bring your own food and drinks on board at no extra cost, though glass bottles are discouraged for safety.

faq.q: Can we swim and use paddle boards?
faq.a: Absolutely. Most boats carry paddle boards and snorkelling gear at no extra charge. Stopping at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés gives you calm, clear water for a refreshing swim. Just ask your skipper to anchor at a suitable spot.

data.body_html:
August in Marbella is glorious: 11 hours of sunshine, sea temperatures around 25°C, and a vibrant Puerto Banús scene. But let's be honest — the heat can be relentless. On land, the mercury often hits 34°C, and even the shade feels warm. The solution? A Marbella boat rental. Out on the Mediterranean, you get a constant sea breeze, the option to dive into cool water whenever you like, and a skipper who knows the best spots to drop anchor. This guide covers how to beat the August heat on the water, which boats to choose, and what it really costs.

Why August is the Perfect Month for a Boat Charter

August is the warmest month in Marbella, with average highs of 31°C and sea water at a balmy 24-26°C. While the beach can feel like a frying pan by midday, a boat offers a natural air-conditioning effect: as you cruise at 20-30 knots, the wind chill drops the perceived temperature by 5-8°C. Plus, you can anchor in the shade of the Sierra Blanca cliffs at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, where the water is glassy and refreshing. The only downside? Everyone knows this, so book early.

Best Boats for Beating the Heat

Not all boats are equal when it comes to staying cool. Here are our top picks for August:

  • Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax): The flybridge offers a shaded upper deck with a bimini top, plus a fully air-conditioned saloon below. Perfect for alternating between sun and shade.
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax): With a huge flybridge and a spacious interior, you can host a group without anyone feeling cramped or overheated. Includes a free jet ski.
  • Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax): The ultimate luxury escape. Her air-conditioned saloon is a cool retreat, and the large swim platform makes getting in and out of the water effortless.
  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax): A budget-friendly option that still has a small cabin with AC — ideal for a midday cool-down.

August Weather in Marbella: What to Expect

In August, Marbella experiences a Mediterranean climate with very little rain (less than 5mm on average). The sea is calm, with swells rarely exceeding 0.5m, so even those prone to seasickness are fine. The terral wind can occasionally blow from the west, pushing temperatures above 36°C — on those days, the sea breeze is even more welcome. Always check the marine forecast before departure; our skippers monitor conditions daily and will advise if any route changes are needed.

How to Stay Cool Onboard: 7 Practical Tips

  1. Book a morning or late afternoon slot — 09:00-13:00 or 16:00-20:00 are cooler and less crowded.
  2. Use the flybridge shade — the upper deck catches the breeze, but the bimini provides essential sun protection.
  3. Take regular swim breaks — anchor at Cala Cortés or Cabopino for a dip; the water is 24-26°C.
  4. Wear lightweight, quick-dry clothing — cotton gets heavy; a rash guard or linen shirt is better.
  5. Stay hydrated — we provide plenty of water, but bring extra if you're a heavy drinker (non-alcoholic, that is).
  6. Use the boat's air conditioning — on flybridge models, the saloon AC is a lifesaver during the hottest hours.
  7. Apply reef-safe sunscreen — SPF 50+ and reapply every 2 hours; the sea reflects UV rays.

All prices include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA. No hidden extras. For other boats like the Canados 86 or Maiora 26m, message us on WhatsApp for a tailored quote.

Where to Go to Escape the Heat

While you can always just cruise the coast, these spots are especially refreshing in August:

  • Cala del Faro — a quiet cove near Cabopino with clear, cool water and shade from the cliffs.
  • Cala Cortés — a favourite for swimming; the water is usually 2-3°C cooler than the open sea.
  • Puerto Banús to Estepona — a 25 NM cruise that passes the sleek beaches of the Golden Mile and ends at Estepona's old town.
  • Río Verde — anchor near the river mouth for a unique backdrop and a quick dip.

What to Wear and Pack for a Summer Charter

Less is more. Bring a swimsuit, a light cover-up, sunglasses with polarised lenses, a hat, and a towel. For footwear, non-slip boat shoes or barefoot is best — heels are a no-go. If you're prone to sunburn, pack a UV-protective shirt and a high-SPF sunscreen. We supply coolers and ice, so your drinks stay cold. And don't forget a waterproof phone pouch for those Instagram shots at the bow.

Book Your Marbella Boat Rental for August 2025

August is our busiest month, and the best boats are reserved weeks in advance. To secure your preferred date, check our availability online or send a WhatsApp message — we typically respond within 30 minutes. If you're flexible, we can also suggest a mid-week charter, which is often calmer and cooler. Beat the heat in style: book your boat today.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the weather like in Marbella in August?

August in Marbella is hot and dry. Expect daytime highs of 30-34°C, with occasional peaks above 36°C. The sea water is warm, around 24-26°C, making swimming very pleasant. The breeze on the water can make it feel 5-8°C cooler than on land.

Which boat is best for staying cool in August?

Flybridge boats like the Azimut 58 Flybridge or the Ferretti 94 are ideal because they offer shaded upper decks with better airflow. The Mangusta 80 also has a large flybridge and a spacious saloon with air conditioning, perfect for escaping the midday sun.

What time of day should I rent a boat in August?

To avoid the peak heat, book a morning charter (9:00-13:00) or a late afternoon one (16:00-20:00). Midday charters are still popular but you'll need to use the boat's shade and take regular swims to cool off.

Are drinks and snacks included on the boat?

Yes, every charter includes water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. You can also bring your own food and drinks on board at no extra cost, though glass bottles are discouraged for safety.

Can we swim and use paddle boards?

Absolutely. Most boats carry paddle boards and snorkelling gear at no extra charge. Stopping at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés gives you calm, clear water for a refreshing swim. Just ask your skipper to anchor at a suitable spot.

How far in advance should I book for August?

August is peak season, so book at least 2-3 weeks ahead, especially for weekends and popular boats like the Mangusta 80. For last-minute bookings, contact us on WhatsApp and we'll check availability for you.

What is the cancellation policy?

Most charters offer free cancellation up to 72 hours before departure. If the weather is dangerous (e.g., storm warnings), we'll reschedule or refund 100%. Check the specific terms when you book.
